chapter: Dew Drop and the club scene
title: Club hopping between the Dew Drop, Foster's and Robin Hood
summary: Clubs were within a few blocks so patrons could walk between them.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: No, but it had an advantage though, because you see, here's what, because when you were not at the Dew Drop you could walk two blocks down and go to Foster and see something like the French Quarter with clubs right next door to one another. So you got a guy who can walk from one area to another and you know, you say, well, you know you get tired of sitting in the same place. You got your lady friend, let's go to another venue and get a drink and let's do our thing and let's get it together. So that's, you know.
Could you walk to Robin Hood? Oh yeah.
Yeah, because the Robin Hood was only what, four or five blocks away. Right, it was right down there on the corner of Jackson Avenue.
So that area you could say, people would, club hop.
Right, club hop. You wouldn't need an automobile. But today's a different one.
